basis: Organic aciduria; intellectual disability and marrow suppression with leukopenia occur in 30-79%. Renal insufficiency annotated 5-29%; respiratory distress can reflect acidosis.
Defined as viral or bacterial infection of the testes; reproductive anatomy has no axis, and endocrine dysfunction is not defining.
Bacterial infection of the endocardium; embolic organ injury is not sufficiently common to add other axes.
T/B-cell immunodeficiency defined by persistent cutaneous infections and eczema. Bronchiectasis (42%) and chronic otitis are separately diagnosed infectious sequelae.
Benign neoplasm of a reproductive organ; no specified skin, urinary, or endocrine origin.
Isolated sperm flagellar abnormalities and male infertility; no endocrine or other axis involvement.
Cutis laxa and intellectual disability (22/23) define the phenotype; osteopenia 10/11 and hip dislocation 15/22 support skeletal involvement. Cataract only 2/22.
Dystonia, progressive cerebellar ataxia and cerebellar atrophy define a neurologic disorder; nystagmus and dysphagia do not establish separate organ damage.
Malignant neoplasm arising in or involving the inner ear.
Isolated spermatogenic failure with oligozoospermia and reduced sperm motility; no demonstrated endocrine dysfunction.
Down syndrome has defining neurodevelopmental impairment; congenital heart defects occur in about 40-50%. Thyroid disease and recurrent otitis are separate diagnoses.
Inherited platelet dysfunction, thrombocytopenia and beta-thalassemia; splenomegaly belongs to the blood axis. Petechiae do not establish skin damage.
Alpha-actin defects cause nemaline skeletal myopathies. Respiratory weakness reflects affected skeletal muscles rather than intrinsic lung disease.
Congenital cleft lip, alveolus and palate affect oral structures, covered by the gastrointestinal axis.
Ancestors and synonym identify hereditary renal disease. Preauricular pits alone do not establish hearing impairment or functional ear damage.
Hereditary colorectal cancer syndrome; other listed malignancies are increased risks and separate diagnoses, not existing organ damage.
Developmental foveal hypoplasia and ocular albinism affect the eye; cutaneous involvement is not established across the group.
Dengue infection with defining vascular leakage and circulatory collapse, plus hemorrhagic disease and thrombocytopenia.
Platelet microthrombi, hemolysis and thrombocytopenia; most cases are autoimmune. Cerebral ischemia/stroke annotated 30-79%; renal insufficiency 5-29%.
Corticospinal and cerebral white-matter disease causes spastic paraplegia. Muscle atrophy reflects neurologic dysfunction rather than a primary muscle lesion.
Well-differentiated tumor arising in the appendix; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine gland disease or hormone dysfunction.
Cloacal and axial duplication affects bowel, urinary tract and vertebrae; spinal cord lesions and myelomeningocele occur in 30-79%. Reproductive anomalies have no axis.
Hereditary persistent speech-fluency disorder, classified under hereditary neurological and developmental speech disorders.
Defining cutaneous and neurologic disease; retinopathy/optic atrophy and hearing impairment each occur in 80-99%. Arteriosclerosis also 80-99%, omitted because of cap.
Hereditary Wilms tumor is a renal embryonal neoplasm; nephroblastoma is the supplied defining phenotype.
